description: Estimate your daily calorie needs with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation and get targets for losing, maintaining or gaining weight.

faqs.a: Mifflin-St Jeor estimates basal metabolic rate (BMR) from sex, age, height and weight. It is considered one of the most accurate general formulas, but it is still an estimate — individual metabolism varies.
faqs.q: What is the Mifflin-St Jeor equation?

faqs.a: Your BMR is multiplied by an activity factor (1.2 for sedentary up to 1.9 for very active) to estimate total daily energy expenditure (TDEE).
faqs.q: How is TDEE different from BMR?

faqs.a: The tool shows TDEE − 500 for weight loss and TDEE + 300 for weight gain — common starting guidelines, not medical advice. Consult a professional before a major diet change.
faqs.q: Where do the lose/gain targets come from?

howto: Select your sex and enter age, height and weight.
Choose the activity level closest to your lifestyle.
Read your BMR and TDEE instantly.
Use the lose / maintain / gain targets as starting guidelines.
title: TDEE Calorie Calculator
